does: Simmers pieces of meat, bird or firm cheese in a gravy made from a fried masala base, with a little water or cream, until they are tender and the gravy has thickened and clings to them.
how: Start from a masala base cooked until its fat has parted.
Add the pieces, raw or already roasted or fried, and stir them into the base for a moment so that they are coated.
Add hot water or cream a little at a time, and bring the pan to a gentle simmer. Cover it partly.
Stir now and then and scrape the bottom. Add a little more liquid if the gravy dries out before the pieces are tender.
Stop when the pieces are tender and the gravy is thick enough to coat them, with a shine of fat on top.
Stir in the finishing touches, such as cream, dried fenugreek leaf or garam masala, off the heat or just before.

cues.text: The gravy is thick and glossy and clings to the pieces, with a little fat shining at the edge.
The pieces give easily under a spoon and are tender throughout.
The scent is round and full, with no raw spice in it.

mistakes.mistake: Pouring in cold water, which stops the cooking and thins the flavour.
mistakes.fix: Add hot water, a little at a time.

mistakes.mistake: Boiling hard, so that the gravy splits and the pieces turn tough.
mistakes.fix: Keep a gentle simmer and stir now and then.

mistakes.mistake: Adding the cream or yogurt to a boiling pan, so that it splits.
mistakes.fix: Take the pan off the heat for a moment, or lower the heat, before the cream goes in.

comes_after.why: The gravy is made on a masala base cooked until its fat parts, so the base comes first.

variant_of.differs: The pieces are not browned first and there is no wine or stock. The liquid is water or cream added to a fried masala base, and the sauce is thick and clings to the pieces. It is cooked on the stove, covered only in part.
